status: Local application choices made for an unofficial companion map atlas of love.fútbol projects, informed by observed website colours and type. Not organization-issued cartography or data standards; love.fútbol has not reviewed or approved them.
scope: Interactive maps of project locations, the administrative areas around them and nearby community facilities. Basemap values, marker meanings, line weights and data rules below are atlas decisions; the palette keys they reuse are observed website colours.

basemap.note: A quiet, warm basemap keeps project markers and the observed brand colours legible. These seven values are atlas choices; they are not part of the observed love.fútbol palette.

layers.label: Admin boundaries
layers.use: Country and state boundary lines on the basemap

labels.note: Country labels in charcoal, other place labels in a slightly softer charcoal, each with an off-white halo.

basemap.starting: The atlas restyles the OpenFreeMap Positron vector style (OpenMapTiles schema).

lens.note: A neighbourhood lens shades three kinds of OpenStreetMap land use from about zoom 11, under the roads, so the facilities around a space read at a glance.

layers.label: Sports pitches
layers.note: OSM pitch, stadium and track land use; white pitch outlines from about zoom 13.

layers.label: Schools
layers.note: School, kindergarten, college and university land use.

markers.label: Project with a profile page
markers.note: A circle with a white stroke. The project number appears in white on the pin at closer zooms.

markers.label: Project known only from the homepage map
markers.note: Same form as a profile pin; the colour says the place has no profile page to open.

markers.label: Cluster of nearby projects
markers.note: A larger terracotta circle with a white count; it expands on selection.

markers.label: Selected space
markers.note: A small top-down pitch with a red corner flag. It is a map symbol, not the logo: never use it as a logo, beside the logo as a lockup, or in place of the complete artwork.

choropleth.label: Countries reached
choropleth.measure: Number of projects with a published location in each country
choropleth.note: A paler tint of light green marks a single project; the ramp reaches green at the maximum. It counts mapped spaces, not people reached.

hierarchy.label: Other levels of the hierarchy
hierarchy.note: Country → state or province → county or region → city → district → neighbourhood. Lines get heavier and darker toward the neighbourhood.

walkRing.label: Walk ring
walkRing.caption: 1 km · about a 12-minute walk
walkRing.note: A straight-line radius, not a measured walking route or a catchment.

type.use: Country names, project names, counters and large numbers
type.basis: Observed website display role (Bahianita spans and counters on the homepage); applied to the atlas by local choice.

type.use: Interface text, labels, legends, sources and captions
type.basis: Observed website body and supporting type.

type.use: The vector style’s own label font
type.basis: Basemap place labels and marker numbers use the tile style’s fonts; they are not set in the brand faces.

photography.rule: Project photographs display in grayscale and return to colour on hover or focus.
photography.basis: The Projects-page photo grid applies a grayscale class to colour images (website-projects-brand-evidence.json). Returning to colour on hover is the atlas’s interaction choice; keep the colour original unchanged and credit every image.

dataHonesty.rule: Treat every coordinate as approximate. Most come from the homepage map, which places some courts at city level; the rest are geocoded from the place named on a profile. Show the source of each coordinate with the space.

Name the source beside every figure: Wikidata, World Bank World Development Indicators, U.S. Census Bureau American Community Survey via Census Reporter, OpenStreetMap. Credit OpenStreetMap contributors and the basemap provider on the map.
Show the year of every population figure. Say when an area has no recorded population rather than estimating one.
Never imply that love.fútbol produced, endorsed or verified third-party statistics. Area statistics describe an administrative area, not the people a space serves or its outcomes.
Quote love.fútbol’s own headline counters as dated, attributed figures. Different pages give different totals; do not reconcile them or recompute them from the map.
Use a project number only where a source gives it, and note conflicts. The homepage map and gallery captions number some projects differently and repeat #52.
